correctness.rationale: Because N is odd, 2 has a modular inverse and the center/difference coordinate pair is bijective. Each non-reset update moves one coordinate ±1 (probability 1/4 each) and leaves the other fixed; absorption is first difference hitting zero. Fourier transforming the center gives a tridiagonal Dirichlet recurrence with parameter alpha=acosh(2/(1-r)-cos k) and explicit cosh-ratio solution. Geometric renewal divides the unreset first-hit Fourier transform by its zero mode. The lazy difference-chain Poisson equations give E[S]=2i(N-i) and the displayed second factorial moment, producing the sharp derivative and correct absence of integer equality. Independent absorbing ordered-pair matrices matched all tested Fourier probabilities and means for N=3,5,7; the finite checks do not extend the universal proof.
residual_risks: Only odd cycles and jointly triggered geometric resetting are treated; even-cycle opposite-parity walkers never collide. The derivative only decides local effect of weak resetting, not unique global optimizer.

value.rationale: Where two particles collide is physically meaningful for reaction placement; a first-collision-anywhere law goes beyond a mean at a prescribed node. The full Fourier law and sharp finite-cycle restart derivative identify an unintuitive parity effect (on C5, reset helps starts two graph steps apart but hinders adjacent ones), so the result is a motivated exact stochastic-transport classification.
